prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks, in which neutral atoms trapped at a magic wavelength brought frequency measurement to the 1e-18 level

statement.case_for: I have moved from the two-part B024 plus B019 configuration to B024 alone. B024 is the most widely supported achievement in the room: four of eight round-1 configurations include it, and every member who comments on its experimental basis calls it solid. It is a measurement-driven advance. Magic-wavelength trapping of thousands of neutral atoms, interrogated Doppler- and recoil-free, removed the old trade-off between atom number and systematic shifts, and clock-to-clock comparisons in several independent laboratories now agree at the 1e-18 level, which is the independent confirmation I ask of any claimed result. The physics will last: centimetre-scale tests of gravitational redshift, searches for varying constants and ultralight dark matter, and the coming redefinition of the second all rest on it. The credit is two names, Katori for the concept and first demonstration and Ye for taking it to record accuracy and many-body clock physics. That is the cleanest attribution on the shortlist. It is also the fallback that Eriksson, Olsson and Mehlig name for their own preferred achievement, so it is the position most likely to survive a full committee discussion.
statement.case_against: B024 sits in a lineage already honoured in 2005 (frequency combs) and 2012 (control of single quantum systems), and the SI redefinition of the second has not yet happened, so a colleague can fairly call it a superb instrument rather than a discovery. SYRTE, PTB, NIST and other groups built much of the systematics programme, and two names cannot reflect that. The 1e-18 figures and the priority history rest on members' recollection and should be checked against the record before the final ballot. A single-achievement prize also leaves out the astroparticle discovery that I still think is real. B019 shows a new observational window, but I cannot support it with the one name the shortlist supplies, and the origin of most of the diffuse flux is unresolved. I am dropping it for that reason and not because the physics is weak.

responses.point: Danielsson keeps B019 as a second part, argues that the 2015 prize concerned oscillation and not neutrinos as cosmic messengers, and says the prize should fall back to B024 alone or B024 plus a different part if Halzen cannot be defended as a sole credit.
responses.response: Your argument against the 2015 overlap is right and I accept it. We also agreed on the test for credit: B019 is the first part to go if Halzen alone cannot be defended. I have now applied it. A one-name credit for a detector with hundreds of builders and analysts reads as unfair, and I cannot add names the shortlist does not support without inventing a credit. You say two more names fit within three laureates, but I do not know which two, and I will not guess at a Nobel credit. If you see a defensible trio that the committee can verify in the record, I would reconsider B019. As things stand I would not split the prize on a credit I do not trust.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B020 as a theory-anticipated, experimentally confirmed platform, names the unresolved pairing mechanism and Yuan Cao's omission as the main weaknesses, and calls B024 the honest alternative.
responses.response: The prediction-then-discovery structure is a strong argument, and I agree the phenomenology is robust across groups. Your point that the citation can be worded around the observed phases and the flat-band prediction, not the mechanism, helps. My reservation is the combination of an eight-year-old field with a three-name credit that leaves out the first author of the 2018 experiments. I rely on you and Olsson for the condensed-matter judgment, so I do not call B020 weak, and I keep it as an alternative because the platform is clearly lasting. Since you name B024 as your fallback, I would like to hear whether you could vote for it as the whole prize this year.

responses.point: Olsson ranked B019 eighth, called Halzen's single-name credit fragile, and supports B020, but says that if the committee cannot be sure the credited people did the original work, B024 is the better-documented alternative.
responses.response: Your objection to Halzen's credit is the strongest argument against my second part, and I have conceded it. Your own test, whether we can be sure the credited people did the original work, seems the right one, and B024 passes it better than anything else on the list: Katori proposed the lattice concept and clock, and Ye's group demonstrated it at record accuracy. I take your point about B020's reproducibility across groups seriously, which is why B020 is my second alternative. The Yuan Cao question does not look resolvable inside the three-name limit, so I would not rank B020 above a mature measurement this year.

responses.point: Kroll argues that the lattice clock gave access to a regime the 2005 and 2012 prizes did not, thousands of atoms interrogated Doppler- and recoil-free at 1e-18, and that the omitted groups are not a reason to withhold the prize.
responses.response: I agree with that distinction and will use it as the working test for the citation: the new capability is large atom number combined with freedom from Doppler and recoil shifts, which neither the comb nor ion control provides. I also accept that the omitted groups do not by themselves block the award, though I would not call the credit fully clean. The 1e-18 numbers and the priority between Katori and contemporaneous groups come from your recollection and mine, and the committee should have an external expert check them. Your year in John Hall's laboratory is a distant tie that you disclosed properly, and I do not think it disqualifies you; the committee should record it.

responses.point: Mehlig moved from B051 to B020, valuing a transparent model prediction tested by experiment, and names the unresolved pairing mechanism and the absent credit for Yuan Cao as the main risks, with B024 as a safer alternative.
responses.response: You were willing to move off your own first choice after reading the room, which is what I have done with B019. The Bistritzer-MacDonald structure is the kind of result I trust. Twist-angle disorder and the pairing question are outside my field, so I cannot judge how far they limit quantitative reproducibility, and I take your caveat about the credit at face value. If you and Eriksson can show that the lasting physics does not hinge on the mechanism, B020 becomes a serious candidate for a later prize. This year I think B024 has the more complete record, and I ask whether you could accept it as the sole part.

responses.point: Johansson asks that the clocks case be argued on the magic-wavelength lattice concept and its realisation at 1e-18, not on the possible redefinition of the second, which he sees as an application.
responses.response: I accept that framing and have written the citation accordingly: the invention and realization of the lattice clock and its 1e-18 performance, with the redefinition only a consequence. On B042, I still cannot judge in depth whether a second superconducting-circuit prize is too close to 2025, so I keep it off my configuration. Your disclosure of direct field overlap is proper, and I support your offer to accept a recusal ruling on the B042 attribution.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can obtain an external expert check of the lattice-clock priority history and the 1e-18 figures before the final ballot, since several of us are working from recollection.
Whether the lineage from 2005 and 2012 and the pending redefinition of the second will cost B024 support in the full committee.
Whether a defensible credit for IceCube exists beyond Halzen alone; if one does, I would revisit B019 as a second part.
Whether B020 is mature enough in a field where I rely on colleagues, and whether the omission of Yuan Cao can be accepted.
Whether a second superconducting-circuit prize (B042) is too close to 2025, which I cannot judge in depth.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for B024. For B019 I work in astroparticle physics (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, XL-Calibur) and have no stated connection to IceCube or Halzen; that field proximity matters less now that I am no longer advancing B019 in my preferred configuration. As Chair I run the process and have tried not to steer colleagues toward B024. If a direct tie to any credited person on B024 or B019 surfaced I would raise recusal.
